stories.title: Lions' Jack Campbell has full movement in lower body after neck injury
stories.summary: Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body as he recovers from a neck injury, suffered in Sunday's game.
stories.detail: Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body as he recovers from a neck injury, suffered in Sunday's game. Campbell, who remains hospitalized, was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter of a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. He was alert and breathing when he was taken to the hospital. "I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," Campbell said in a statement. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." Lions coach Dan Campbell said it was powerful that Jack Campbell updated his improving condition himself, shortly before the team's previously scheduled news conferences with coaches and players. teamStories.detail: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders are beginning their practice week Wednesday to prepare for Sunday’s game at the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers and, has been the case for most of the season, appear to be close to full health. According to multiple reports, the only starter not on the practice field at the beginning of Wednesday’s session was outside cornerback Darien Porter. That is not a surprise since Porter departed Sunday’s 38-33 win at the New York Jets on the first play from scrimmage with a groin injury. He did not return. Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Porter would be monitored as the week progressed. If he can’t play Sunday, rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses will likely rotate as they did against the Jets. The only other player not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice was reserve wide receiver Cody White. Starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was on the field Wednesday. He played just 13 snaps Sunday because of a stinger. stories.title: Warriors withholding payments to Porzingis, sources say
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services.
stories.detail: The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services. General manager Mike Dunleavy and the Warriors' front office are still actively pursuing trade avenues utilizing Porzingis' contract even as the 31-year-old leans toward ending his NBA career. For rival teams, absorbing Porzingis' near-expiring salary could either allow them to move a longer-term salary out to save money (plus clear a roster spot via buyout) or theoretically net a draft asset, depending on what the Warriors are willing to attach. The Warriors have no current plans on voiding Porzingis' contract, team sources said, maintaining trade flexibility up until the Feb. 11 deadline. Porzingis is not actively disputing the lack of payments and the player's association has no plan to dispute either, league sources said. Under different circumstances last season, the Miami Heat withheld payments for veteran guard Terry Rozier while he was under federal investigation in a gambling scandal but did spend the months leading up to the deadline exploring trad…

stories.title: Dumont family takes full control of Mavericks, buying Miriam Adelson's shares
stories.summary: Little will change on the ground as Patrick Dumont has been the team governor and running the show already.
stories.detail: Patrick and Sivan Dumont have formally become the controlling owners of the Dallas Mavericks after purchasing Miriam Adelson's shares of the franchise last month, a story broken by Tim MacMahon of ESPN . The Dumonts now own 69% of the Mavericks. While this is a change at the top, it should have little day-to-day impact, as Patrick Dumont has served as team governor and been the acting owner on the ground since the day Mark Cuban sold the team to the Dumonts and Adelsons. Here is what Dumont told ESPN: "It's really about long-term investment in the city of Dallas," Dumont told ESPN on Tuesday. "The Dumont family is really committed to building what we hope is the best arena in the NBA, a really significant investment in the city that will help create the new 40-year home for the Dallas Mavericks, a great experience for our fans and inspire our team to win championships. That's really what we're focused on. We had the opportunity, and we're really excited about it." As Cuban said when he sold his majority share of the team, the NBA has become a real estate business, and what Dumont is looking to build is not just a new arena but the anchor of a much larger development. teamStories.detail: Oct 12, 2024; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Jeremy Sochan (10) in the second half against the Utah Jazz at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con When the Spurs first drafted Jeremy Sochan out of Baylor with the 9th overall pick in 2022, I remember probably being more thrilled with the pick than warranted. I hardly knew anything about him, but I did know he had size and was not a guard, and that’s all I wanted. If you ignore 2019 (when the Spurs drafted a bust power forward in Luka Samanic and a truly “small” forward in Keldon Johnson) and 2015 (when they drafted and stashed center Nikola Milutinov), you otherwise had to go all the way back to 2014 and Kyle Anderson to find the last time they drafted a player who was not a guard or small wing in the first round. (And even then, Anderson was more of a guard in a forward’s body.) As good as some of those picks were — steals with Dejounte Murray and Derrick White late in the first round, Devin Vassell as their first lottery pick since Tim Duncan — others were merely okay or even complete busts that failed to address what was constantly an area of weakness …

(Jerome and the Cavaliers would win the title the next season.) He played two seasons with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Oklahoma City . He played one season with Stephen Curry in Golden State . Something front offices around the league are surely aware of by now: Jerome can become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Jerome, a starting guard for ESPN's Contract Year All-Stars, headlines a 12-player roster full of potential impact free agents, many of whom are searching for massive paydays in the 2027 offseason.
